text:
Maya: quick q about the embeddings endpoint behavior — I'm trying to nail down the contract for mixed batches. If a client sends a batch like [\"hello\", \"\", null, \"world\"] what do we currently guarantee around: order, returned vector count/shape, how null/empty are handled, and any truncation/warnings?

Liam: short answer: we preserve order and return an entry per input. but there are some nuances. writing up details below so we can lock API doc text.

Ben: tagging infra-bot to confirm runtime behavior on token-truncation and batch limits @infra-bot :eyes:

infra-bot: FYI current runtime behavior (prod canaries): 1) we enforce a soft per-request token budget (model-specific, e.g. 8192 tokens default) 2) we cap item count to 2048 by default (configurable per deployment) 3) when an input exceeds token limit we truncate to model limit and set per-item metadata flagged truncated=true in internal trace. (no user-facing header today).

Maya: thanks — for the client contract, do we want to return the per-item truncated flag in the response body? customers ask for explicit signals.

Irene: I'd prefer including a per-item field instead of relying on headers. e.g. data[i].truncated = true/false. That keeps alignment obvious.

Kai: agreed on alignment. current responses include an ordered data array with index fields. proposal: data array length == inputs.length and each item is either {index:int, embedding:[float], truncated:bool} or {index:int, error:string} for invalid inputs.

Maya: ok — what about null vs empty-string? If a caller passes JSON null should we treat it as an empty string, or return an error for that slot?

Liam: current impl treats JSON null as an explicit empty input (same as empty string) and returns the model's embedding for empty string. We do not convert null -> remove slot. This preserves alignment. We also accept and embed whitespace-only strings (we trim for tokenization but still produce an embedding).

Ben: note: some downstream customers expect null -> null (no vector) so they can detect missing entries. If we always return embedding for null, they'll need to check for e.g. zero-vector which is ambiguous. Do we ever produce exact zero-vector? not intentionally.

Irene: we should not return synthetic zero-vectors unless model outputs that. Better: if input is invalid (non-string non-null), return data[i].error = \"invalid input type\" and embedding omitted. For JSON null we'll opt to treat as empty string. That maps to current runtime behavior.

Maya: can we add a small example snippet for docs and SDKs?

Kai: example request (curl):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "rwd-embedding-1536",
  "input": ["hello", "", null, "world"]
}
```
example response (proposed contract):
```
{
  "model":"rwd-embedding-1536",
  "input_length":4,
  "data":[
    {"index":0, "embedding":[0.012, -0.34, ...], "truncated":false},
    {"index":1, "embedding":[0.001, -0.02, ...], "truncated":false},
    {"index":2, "embedding":[0.001, -0.02, ...], "truncated":false},   // null treated as empty string
    {"index":3, "embedding":[0.10, 0.003, ...], "truncated":false}
  ]
}
```
Notes: embeddings are fixed-length floats (length depends on model, e.g. 1536). order preserved by index. we also include input_length top-level for quick checks.

Ben: how do we indicate per-item errors (e.g. non-string object)? proposed: {"index":N, "error":"invalid input type"} and omit embedding. consumers can filter by presence of embedding.

Maya: what about partial truncation warning for large text? Kai mentioned per-item truncated flag. good. Do we also want a top-level warning header for when any item got truncated?

Irene: top-level warnings are nice for analytics, but per-item flag is required for correctness. We can include both: top-level warnings: ["truncated_items: 2"] and/or `meta.truncated_count`. But keep it optional in first pass.

Liam: batch limits — we should make docs say: both per-item token limit and total token budget apply. If total tokens exceed budget we try to accept items until budget is exhausted and then return 413-like error with `error: "batch token budget exceeded"`. We do NOT silently drop trailing items.

Maya: good — explicit failure is easier for clients. For SDKs we can provide automatic chunking helpers though.

DocsBot: created draft PR: docs/embeddings/contract/embeddings-batch-behavior.md with the proposed JSON examples and the per-item fields. Link: https://stash.internal/docs/embeddings/PR-742 :book:

Maya: tl;dr action items — @Kai to update runtime to surface truncated boolean in response for canary; @Irene + @Ben to write error case wording; @Liam to update SDKs to treat null as empty-string and preserve ordering; @DocsBot to land docs PR. I can take a follow-up to add example SDK code showing how to filter for errors.

Kai: I'll open a small runtime change request today, will add unit tests for null/empty and for token-truncation flag.

Ben: will draft the exact error message strings we should use in the next 24h.

Maya: perfect, thanks all :rocket:
